Property Mutation Creation in Hyderabad

Registration transfers the deed; mutation transfers the record. We update the revenue and municipal records into your name after a purchase, inheritance or gift.

Key Takeaways

  • Mutation updates the government's revenue or municipal records to show you as the current owner.
  • It is separate from registration — you can hold a registered deed and still not be mutated.
  • Mutation is required after purchase, inheritance, gift or partition, and to pay property tax in your name.
  • For agricultural land it flows through the state land-records system; for urban property through GHMC/municipality.
  • We prepare, file and follow up the mutation end to end.

When you buy, inherit or receive property, registering the deed is only half the job. The government's records — the ones used for property tax and future sales — must also be updated to your name. That update is called mutation.

JaaGa handles the full mutation: preparing the application, filing it with the correct revenue or municipal office, and following it through to the updated record.

When Mutation Is Required

After buying a property, so the revenue/municipal record and property-tax liability move into your name.

After inheritance, gift or partition — and whenever the seller's own mutation was never completed, which must be fixed before yours.

The Mutation Process

  1. 1

    Document Review

    We review your registered deed, prior records and identity documents to confirm mutation eligibility.

  2. 2

    Application Filing

    We file the mutation application with the correct office — land records for agricultural land, GHMC/municipality for urban property.

  3. 3

    Verification

    We coordinate the field/record verification by the revenue or municipal officer.

  4. 4

    Approval & Updated Record

    On approval, the record is updated and we deliver your mutated extract / updated record.

Documents Required

  • Registered sale/gift/partition deed
  • Prior title document / link deed
  • Identity and address proof
  • Latest property-tax receipt (for urban property)
  • Death certificate & legal heir proof (for inheritance)

Common Problems We Solve

Seller never mutated

If the previous owner's mutation is missing, yours can't proceed. We fix the chain first.

Record mismatches

Name or extent mismatches between deed and record stall mutation. We reconcile them.

Inheritance without a will

Intestate succession needs legal-heir proof. We guide and assemble the required documents.

Why Property Mutation Creation Matters

Until mutation is done, the government still treats the previous owner as the record-holder — which blocks property-tax updates, complicates future sales and can expose you to disputes. Completing mutation is what makes your ownership visible in the records that matter.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is registration the same as mutation?

No. Registration records the deed at the SRO; mutation updates the revenue/municipal records to show you as owner. Both are needed.

How long does mutation take in Hyderabad?

It varies by property type and office workload — typically a few weeks once documents are in order. We follow up throughout.

Can NRIs get mutation done remotely?

Yes. Share your documents on WhatsApp and we handle filing and follow-up; a signature or POA may be required for some steps.

What if the seller's mutation was never done?

That gap must be closed before your mutation. We assess the chain and complete the missing step.

Do I need mutation to pay property tax in my name?

Yes — property tax records follow the mutated owner, so mutation is what puts the tax liability and receipts in your name.
